beats.text: One database for writes and reads?
beats.say: One database serving both writes and reads has to compromise. The same schema, the same load, for two very different jobs.
CQRS splits the system in two: commands that change data, and queries that read it.
A command is validated, checked against the business rules, then written to the write model.
The change is published as an event, which updates the read model, shaped exactly for the screens that need it.

beats.text: Queries: fast reads. Scale each side separately.
beats.say: Queries just read those ready-made views, fast, with no joins and no business logic. And you can scale reads and writes separately.

beats.text: The catch: eventual consistency, two models.
beats.say: The catch: the read side is eventually consistent, and you now run two models. Use it when your reads and writes really differ.
